<reason>B established why private unprofitability need not imply poor public value, then defended a selective, technology-neutral subsidy policy. A raised legitimate appraisal, capture, and opportunity-cost concerns, but B answered with reviewable outcomes, conservative assumptions, and lifetime costing. A repeatedly treated uncertainty as grounds for automatic refusal while relying on uncertain future coverage. Its closing also falsely characterized B as conceding that appraisal cannot address error and misread “even when” as requiring funding whenever carriers decline.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B distinguished construction costs from operating costs and showed that vouchers either leave the construction gap unresolved or become expansion subsidies themselves. A conceded that an operationally sustainable network can remain unbuilt, then raised demand risks without defeating that financing mechanism. This substantially weakened A’s proposed alternative.</best_rebuttal>
